Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the quick response on the RFP. We reviewed Redwood's hosting modes and would love a focused 30–40 minute demo next week to validate latency and multi-tenant fallbacks.

Attaching a short agenda and our availability window (PST): Mon 7/31 10:00–12:00, Tue 8/1 13:00–15:30, Wed 8/2 09:00–11:00. We prefer Meet but Zoom is fine.

A couple of constraints: our calendar admin enforces consent propagation from external organizers, and last time an invite forwarded through our SSO stripped the join button. If possible, can you send the invite from a Redwood user with an explicit backup Zoom link in the body?

Thanks —
Annie

ElevateOps

Hi Annie —

Great to meet you virtually. Thanks for the availability — we can do Tue 8/1 at 13:30 PST. I'll send the calendar invite from my account and include a Zoom fallback link in the event description. Laura (CS) will run the product walkthrough and Ben (Solutions) will cover integration notes.

Quick note: I tried attaching the .ics from our scheduling tool but it looks like the forwarded .ics loses the "X-GOOGLE-CONSENT" field in some tenant flows. To avoid that, I'll first send a plain Gmail invite, then follow up with an email containing the Zoom join URL and an inline shortlink. That usually prevents the join button from being stripped by proxy SSO.

Proposed plan (short):
- I’ll create the canonical Meet invite (organizer: sergio@redwood.com).
- Immediately after, I’ll send a follow-up with the Zoom backup and a regenerated .ics attached labeled "elevateops-ics.ics".
- If you still see missing join UI, Ben will open the alternative moderator bridge from our account.

Do you prefer we list the backup Zoom as "Join (Zoom backup)" in the event description or as a separate calendar attachment?

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
